entity_noun: product of the business's own design

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it:

rules.text: At least one {{entity_noun}} can be identified from the text — a tangible good, or line of goods, rather than a service, a capability, or a kind of work performed on other parties' goods.

The text says something substantive about the identified {{entity_noun}} — describing an activity, arrangement, or dealing that involves it — rather than only naming it, listing it as a topic, or mentioning it in passing. Which party is involved is not this condition's subject; [PRD-3] and [PRD-4] decide that.

What the identified {{entity_noun}} is — its design, specification, formulation, or composition — originates with and belongs to this business, rather than being supplied or dictated by the party that buys it.

children.text: A good the business designed remains its own even when it is made for another party or sold under that party's name; what settles this condition is whose design it is, not whose name it carries.

rules.text: It is this business that produces the identified {{entity_noun}} — in an operation it runs — rather than having another party produce it and offering the result as its own.

children.text: Production by a division of the same business, or at a site the business operates, counts as this business; goods bought in finished and re-branded or resold do not.

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} is ruled out if ANY of these guards is violated by it. Ruling out one candidate does not settle the classification — another candidate may still qualify:

rules.text: The business's engagement with the identified {{entity_noun}} is only planned, in development, or discontinued, rather than current and actual.
